summary.intent: Triage and fix open review findings on monokl PRs, record outcomes in Entire, then bring PR #45 up to date with main by merging and resolving conflicts.
summary.outcome: Review fixes were pushed to PR 48, 6 of 9 findings fixed and resolved and 3 dismissed with verified facts. A broken 0.3.0 release was found and PR #49 opened to fix it. Main was merged into PR #45's branch with three conflicts resolved, and all gates passed (758 tests, lint, doc-check, typos, drift check, strict changeset validation). The signed merge commit was made, but the transcript does not show it being pushed.

repo: Callisto 0.17 refuses to plan or release from a branch checkout (E170: requires a detached HEAD), and its generated workflow checks out the branch. The release workflow's plan and execute jobs need `ref: ${{ github.sha }}`.
The failed 0.3.0 release means no monokl@0.3.0 tag or GitHub release exists and crates.io is still at 0.2.0. `callisto release pending` still lists 0.3.0 as unfinished.

The decision log at docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md uses numbered sections that are cross-referenced from other docs, such as docs/architecture/query-and-ranking.md. Renumbering a section means retargeting every reference to it.
PR #43 changed `FileAnalysis`, which affects PR #45's tests, so the merged tree must be compiled and tested, not just textually merged.
Project gates include the full test suite, lint, doc-check, typos, drift check and strict changeset validation. Each cargo command is run separately.
There is no Windows target, which was the basis for dismissing the Windows-path finding.
`SearchLimits` is slated for removal in trail 189, which makes the unused library clamp moot.
workflow: Merge main into the PR branch (no rebase, no force-push) and use signed commits when updating an existing PR.
Verify a finding's premise before acting on it. The 'already-released behaviour' finding was dismissed because 0.3.0 was never published.
Comparing a generated template to an older version by eye is unreliable. Regenerating with the tool's `init` and diffing is more trustworthy.
For large section reorders in conflict resolution, a short script is safer than retyping the long text.
An Entire trail URL maps to a PR (trail 187 is PR #45).

friction: The push to PR 48 needed a retry.
Merging main into #45 produced three conflicts (README.md, pipeline/mod.rs, the decision log), and the decision-log conflict also caused five stale section-number references.
The earlier survey wrongly concluded the 0.17 release template was unchanged from 0.14, so the release breakage went undetected until triage.
open_items: Decide how to recover or re-release 0.3.0 after #49 merges: either a new release PR that publishes 0.4.0 and skips 0.3.0, or a manual recovery of 0.3.0.
The execute-job detached checkout in #49 is untested until a real release runs.
If 0.3.0 is recovered exactly as that commit, the changesets in #48 may need to be dropped or moved.
The user still needs to decide on non-UTF-8 handling and parent-ignore-file behaviour.
The Entire Gates and code-owner review settings are still undecided.
The merge commit on #45 still needs to be pushed to the PR branch.
Read the rendered changelog in the next release PR.
